impl.summary: H3 Person Remover is now mask-first, reviewable and one click from where people are. A green-mask preview runs the removal graph's own SAM 3.1 chain on the part's first 2 s, with the mask expansion and the person's words editable. Each finished 22-frame window keeps H3 Relay's checkpoint and preview, and 'Redo from here' redraws a window with a new seed while every window before it comes back exactly. This uses the Relay's own Review Windows controls through the ComfyUI provider. There is a new Video tools tab 'Remove a person', a 'Remove a person' entry in a video's menu in the Library and feed and in a Cinema take's menu, a remove_person Assist/MCP tool, and a GPU pre-flight row. Both graphs validate on the live CPU ComfyUI, which has the h3-relay pack. Not built: the cloud route (no hosted green-fill step), the Canvas node and the Character Swap Studio Finish stage.

src/server/providers/comfyui.ts: for the H3 removal graph, the provider records the run's ComfyUI input names and save prefix in meta.reviewInputs. After a run it reads the h3_removal_run UI output, fetches the Relay's run manifest and adds meta.review to the video output, with the window previews in meta.artifacts, which persistArtifacts keeps.

findings.title: Window previews are never kept on a local or LAN ComfyUI, so every window shows 'No preview'
findings.detail: withRemovalReview stores each window's preview as a raw `${baseUrl}/view?...` link in meta.artifacts and relies on persistArtifacts → keepLink → fetchRemoteToFile to copy it. That fetcher uses blockedForLinks by default, which refuses loopback and private addresses unless FUOBE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=1. It also sends no ComfyUI Authorization header. The default install (COMFYUI_URL http://127.0.0.1:8188, or a LAN box) therefore never keeps a preview. The raw internal ComfyUI URLs stay in meta.artifacts, keepLink logs a warning for each window, and the WindowReview grid (which only renders /api/files/ or data: links) shows 'No preview' for every window. The implementer's 'left' only names the comfyToken case; the private-address case breaks it on the most common setup. Redo still works, but item 1 of the brief ('show each finished window's preview') does not work in practice.
findings.evidence: Ran fetchRemoteToFile('http://127.0.0.1:8188/system_stats', …, {}) from the branch with node --conditions=react-server: 'REFUSED: Fuobe won't fetch 127.0.0.1:8188: it points to this machine or a private network.' keepLink calls it with {} for the owner (generations.ts:2298).
findings.fix: Download the previews inside the provider, the way bundleFrames does for EXR frames: comfyFetch/outputFetch with authHeaders, then adoptFile into /api/files. Store those URLs in meta.artifacts, never raw ComfyUI links. Add a test that a review from a 127.0.0.1 ComfyUI ends up with /api/files links.

findings.title: Window review and 'Redo from here' only exist in the run panel of the current page visit; Assist promises otherwise

findings.evidence: grep setRun: only lines 253 (start) and 562 (onRedo). The history section is <Feed items={history.data!} />.

findings.title: Reroll edge cases: inputs re-uploaded every time, and no sound when the original mux never filled its audio
findings.detail: (a) The reroll resends erase.request.inputs: the fitted video and the clean frame. The provider uploads both to ComfyUI under new nanoid names and then replaces them with the reuse names, so each redo leaves two orphaned uploads in ComfyUI's input folder. (b) The reroll copies only mux.request.inputs.audio. When the part isn't the whole clip, that audio was chained from the 'sound' trim and is written into the stored request only when the mux actually started. If the original mux was cancelled or failed before filling (for example, its sound step failed), the redo's mux has no audio input and fails.
findings.evidence: uploadTo names each upload fuobe_${nanoid(8)}; joinWithSound chains audio from 'sound' when not wholeClip; the reroll's final step has inputs only if mux.request.inputs?.audio.
findings.fix: Skip uploading when reuse applies. For (b), re-chain the original sound step's output, or refuse with a clear reason.

findings.title: Report inaccuracy: linked-GPU runs do get a review
findings.detail: reviewInputs is recorded for every H3 removal, regardless of ownGpu, computerScope or tenantAccount; only the reuse override is gated. withRemovalReview then runs for an account's linked ComfyUI too: it fetches /h3_relay/removal/previews there, and persistArtifacts copies the previews into the account's files, within account limits and blockedForAccounts. This is harmless: accounts get 403 on /reroll and can't reach the tool's RunPanel. But the 'left' note ('a computer or linked-GPU run carries no review') is wrong. On the owner's computer or workers, comfyFetch throws and is caught, so those runs have no review.
findings.evidence: In prepareWorkflow, `if (typeof values.video === 'string' && …) reviewInputs = …` sits outside the `own` check. The call site at line 2347 is unconditional for the H3 manifest.
findings.fix: Gate reviewInputs (and so the review) on `own`, or fix the docs note.

findings.title: Regenerated shared data carries unrelated churn
findings.detail: object_info.subset.json was re-dumped from the live server. It adds 6 FuobeLive node definitions (another package's live area) and changes 32 others (H3CharacterSwap*, REUSE*, LTX IC-LoRA, MiniMaxH3TurboLoRA, DA3/MoGe, RemeshMesh) beyond the H3 Relay nodes this package needs. As a side effect, requirements.json flips the LTX-2.5 restore LoRA from presence 'list' to 'loader'. Separately, comfy-library-4.test.ts *removes* an id from the exact unvalidated list. The rules allow only adding new ids there, although the edit is forced by the graph now validating and is reported in 'left'. Expect merge conflicts with packages built in parallel.
findings.evidence: Python diff of the object_info subset against the base: added 6, changed 32, removed 0.
findings.fix: Limit the subset rebuild to the node classes this package's graphs use, or flag the extra churn for the integration merge.

findings.title: Small UI and accessibility issues in WindowReview
findings.detail: Each button's aria-label 'Redo from window N' replaces its visible text 'Redo from here' (WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name). 'Redo from here' is enabled on windows whose earlier windows have no checkpoint, so the server always refuses them; the button could be disabled using rerollProblem client-side. In person mode, if H3 Person Removal is switched off in Models & licences, the 'Remove a person' tab quietly falls back to VACE with no note.
findings.fix: Use visible text that contains the label (e.g. 'Redo from window N'), disable the button with a tooltip from rerollProblem, and show a note when the person eraser is off.

An upstream canvas node's result has none of these until it runs. A proper node also needs a new node type, a palette entry, a settings UI (who to remove, mask expansion), a NodeStep plan and canvas tests, which is beyond a fix pass.
